key_insight: Symmetry-preserving quantum circuits can still be trapped in invariant subspaces, but residual-algebra analysis identifies added generators that unlock target-state accessibility.
engineering_relevance: Screening symmetry-preserving gates before optimization can reveal unreachable targets and guide circuit extensions that remove structural barriers.
method: Compute the residual algebra and its commutant to identify invariant blocks and fidelity bounds.
Screen added generators by the blocks they couple and the adjoint modules they generate.
Use real-rotation and complex-escape criteria to expand controllability; connect multiple blocks through a low-cost spanning tree.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports algebraic proofs and demonstrations in XXZ and Hubbard models, where screened circuit extensions remove identified accessibility obstructions.
watch_item: Removing algebraic accessibility barriers does not by itself guarantee shallow circuits, noise robustness, or successful variational optimization.
paper_title: Residual-Algebraic Design of Symmetry-Preserving Variational Quantum Circuits
